span.span: Decision: competition
# source: scripts/train_agora.py:1221-1247,1468-1509 (_L3_DECISION_INSTRUCTIONS, _llm_decide_l3; called from run_l3_gate_single_check:1512-1583)
# condition: competition (--l3-gate-mode single_check; end of every training step)
# {chairman_name} = the current chairman, i.e. the role holding Tier 1 after the
# previous step’s competition rotation. Before this call, any proposal whose
# pool.yaml would name a different chairman is dropped
# (reason "chairman_set_by_competition_tiers").
=== PROMPT (user message) ===

You are {chairman_name}, the team’s chairman, holding the role because your contribution scored highest. This step your team collected the structural changes listed below; teammate reviews are attached as reference. You alone decide which to adopt. Weigh the reviews, but the call is yours. Keep or drop each proposal and order the kept ones by priority.
Proposals:
{proposal_list}

Reply with ONLY a JSON object: {"keep": [indices of proposals to keep], "order": [the kept indices, highest priority first]}. Example: {"keep": [2, 0], "order": [2, 0]}. An empty keep list is allowed.
=== FORMAT OF EACH ENTRY IN {proposal_list} (entries separated by a blank line) ===
[{index}] {unit_label}
proposed_by: {proposed_by}
reason: {target_file}: {reason}; {target_file_2}: {reason_2}
teammate reviews:
- {teammate_name}: "{challenge_reflection_comment}"
- {teammate_name}: (no response)
(If a proposal has no reviews at all, the review block is the single line
" teammate reviews: (none)".)
{unit_label} is one of: "add <role>" (new role: its config.yaml + prompt.md as one
unit), "remove <role>", "patch <role>" (config.yaml and/or prompt.md of an existing
role), "patch constitution.md", "patch pool.yaml".
=== CALL / RESPONSE HANDLING ===
One single-turn user message (no system prompt) on the chairman’s own model
(the `model:` of <chairman>/config.yaml), temperature 0.0, max_tokens 300.
Expected response: {"keep": [...], "order": [...]} (a bare JSON list is also
accepted and read as keep, in order). If the reply cannot be parsed, every
proposal is kept in arrival order. Kept proposals are then capped in this
order (max 2 add/remove units, max 2 patch groups per step) and tested together
in ONE paired held-out check (current team vs. changed team, same tasks); the
changes are applied unless the changed team is clearly worse (one-sided
binomial test, alpha = 0.3; not applied if either side has fewer than 10
sessions that complete without crashing).
